main_text.p: MEDICUS quibus necessarius, Matt. 9. 11. Marc. 2. 17. Luc. 5. 31. medico honos tribuendus, Eccles. 38. 1. Locus dandus v. 12. medicinæ magis quàm Deo fidere perniciosum. Exemplum Asa, 2. Paral. 16. 12. medice cura teipsum, Luc. 4. 13. Verum medicus Christus: Mat. 11. 28. V. Col. 4. 14. Lucas medicus Col. 4. 14.

MEDIA inconcessa quærentium exempla: Saul, 1. Sam. 28. v. 6. 7. 8. Ochosias, 2. Reg. 1. v. 2. 3. 4. Rex Moabitarum, 3. 27. Zambri, 1. Reg. 16. 18. Asa plus fidit medicis, quam Deo, 2. Para. 16. 13. Achaz, 28. v. 3. 4. Ephraim, Oseæ 5. 13. mediis (quas vocant) legitimis utentes iuuat Deus, 2. Sam. 10. 12. 2. Para. 32. v. 6. 8. Nehem. 4. 9. 21.
MEDITANDVM verbum Dei, Deut. 11. verf. 18. 19. Iosu. 1. 8. Psalm. 1. 2. Psalm. 18. 15. sit meditatio animi mei coram te.
MEDI ad vastandam Babyloniam à Deo excitati, Esai. 13. v. 17. 18. Dan. 5. 28. occupant eam. v. 31. V. Act. 2. 9. Media autem regio est Asiæ maioris.

MEL in corpore leonis, Iudic. 14. 8. sit mel de petra surgerent, constituit Deus Israelitas super excelsam terram, Deut. 32. 13. mel gustat Ionathas, edicti paterni ignarus, 1. Sam. 14. 27. Mel agreste alimentum I. I. Matt. 3. 4.

MELCHISEDECH Rex & Sacerdos, Gen. 14. 18. Ps. 110. 4. Heb. 7. 1. Christus typus: Primùm in coniunctione Regni & Sacerdotij, Heb. 7. 1. Secundò, in adiunctis Regni, pace, & iustitia, v. 2. Tertiò, quia principio & fine careat, v. 3. Quartò, quia Abrahamo superior, v. 4. 5. 6. 7. Melchisedechi lacerdotium præstantius est quàm Leviticum, 7. v. 6. 7. (1. Rex iustus sue iustitiæ.)
MELLO ambitus montis Sion interior, in quem populus conuenire solebat, ædificatur à Salomone, 1. Reg. 9. 24. Iud. 9. 6.

MEMBRA, pro omnibus hominis partibus, Iac. 4. 1. ea sunt mortificanda, Coloss. 3. 5. Membrorum vocabulo Paulus eleganter vocat pravos illos motus, & cupiditates spiritui repugnantes, atque adeò totam hominis non regeneratam partem, Coloss. 3. 5. (Vide CARO : & HOMO) Membra nostra Templum Spiritus Sancti, 1. Corinth. 6. 19. V. Eph. 4. 16. Sumus alii aliorum membra, v. 25. V. Cor. 12. 25.
MEMBRANAS adferri sibi cupit Paulus, 2. Tim. 4. 13.

page.notes: Page is a photographed open book; the facing page at the right edge is show-through and is omitted. Several words in the scan are blurred or damaged by the binding and by the gutter at the left, and readings such as "Lucas medicus", "Mel agreste" and the Greek-free citations were read with some uncertainty. The running head is printed "MED MEL MEM".
